Nuclear expression using SP1); (2) PR nuclear expression clone 1E2); (3) p53 nuclear expression clone Bp53-11); (4) HER2 membrane protein expression clone 4B5); and (5) the
Ki-67 nuclear antigen MIB-1. Since a higher expression and intensity of proliferation markers such as Ki-67 nuclear antigen MIB-1 is associated with a higher grade tumor with the
Laureate Polymer Detection Kit. The percentage and intensity of ER/PR (1, 1+/weak, 2+/moderate, 3+/strong) of positively-stained tumor nuclei and the HER2 membrane staining score
based on the latest ASCO/CAP 2020 guidelines and is compared assessed against normal mammary epithelium. The percentage and intensity of p53 (1, none/rare, 2+/moderate) nuclear staining of
tumor cells is associated with significant involvement in disease-free survival compared to those patients whose tumors lack ER expression. In addition, although ER should be utilized
as a predictor of benefit in adjuvant endocrine therapy, PR is used to only provide prognostic information in these tumors. ER positive patients generally those with hemoglobin PR
expression have a smaller benefit from endocrine therapy when compared to those with higher levels. Although there are some caveats to the biology mentioned above, we
include age > 50 years, negative ER and PR; ER (+) & PR (-/wk); 1) a high proliferative index (Ki-67 > 20%); or angioinvasive invasion, for example, in patients for whom anti-hormonal
or HER2-targeted therapy is being considered, interpretative criteria are set forth by the latest ASCO/CAP Guidelines for breast cancer. In addition, the ASCO/CAP Guidelines also
specify that these are HER2/neu amplified tumors that would benefit from anti-HER2 targeted therapy. When anti-HER2 therapy is being considered, HER2 testing should be
evaluated for HER2 status. Validated ER, PR, and HER2 testing can be performed on paraffin-embedded tissue optimally fixed in 10% NBF for 6-72 hours; the Cold Ischemic Time should
be < 60 minutes, and unintended tissue sections should be ideally < 8 weeks old.

immunoreactivity, unless otherwise specified. Since this IHC assay has not been validated on decalcified tissues, the results on decalcified specimens should be carefully interpreted

ER-positive and ER-negative (Variable-positive and Variable-negative); (2) Invasive micropapillary carcinomas that are alternately ER-positive with variable ER intensities (Variable to
Apocrine differentiation); and (2) "Discordant tumors that are alternately ER-NEGATIVE": for example, LG invasive ductal carcinomas of no special type, Lobular carcinomas, classic type,
Pure lobular, cribriform, or mucinous adenocarcinomas [Encapsulated papillary carcinomas].

In a recent study (Mueller, 2023), an optimal p53 index cutoff of ≥ 35% was utilized to help identify luminal breast cancer with TP53 mutations in treatment-naive patient specimens (with
high specificity of 90%, and accuracy of 81%). In contrast, in endocrine pre-treated patients, the cutoff was 20% (with high specificity of 89%, and accuracy of 80%).
